name: San Juan River
gaugeName: San Juan River near Bluff, UT
blurb: Sand Island to Mexican Hat (Upper San Juan) and the Goosenecks / Mexican Hat to Clay Hills (Lower San Juan). BLM permit required year-round.

sections.notes: BLM permit required year-round (recreation.gov lottery). BLM trip planner: 27 miles, typically 2-3 days; river has class II to III rapids. River left (south) is Navajo Nation - separate permit to camp/hike. Do not leave vehicles overnight at Mexican Hat (break-ins).

guideTimes.conditions: BLM typical trip-length guidance. Includes overnight itinerary planning; actual time varies with conditions, camps and permit requirements.
guideTimes.sourceName: BLM San Juan Trip Planning Information

putInAccess.note: Imagery: the BLM point (and BLM page coordinate) is in the staging lot near the ranger station, about 40 m from the nearest bank and about 75 m from the launch beach. Too far from the water to pass the imagery check. Official source names boating access, but the exact water-entry point is not pinned by an agency coordinate confirmed on imagery. Restrictions: permit-required
putInAccess.directions: Sand Island Recreation Site (BLM) near Bluff; launch beach below the ranger station.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: BLM: San Juan River Trip Planning Information
takeOutAccess.note: Imagery: the BLM point is at the entrance of the gravel launch area, about 50-55 m from the water. Too far from the water to pass. Official source names boating access, but the exact water-entry point is not pinned by an agency coordinate confirmed on imagery. Restrictions: permit-required; vehicle-break-ins
takeOutAccess.directions: Mexican Hat launch (BLM), upstream of the US-163 bridge.

sections.notes: BLM: 57 miles, typically 4-5 days; Government Rapid often requires scouting. Clay Hills is the only viable take-out; BLM warns of a dangerous waterfall downstream of Clay Hills - do not miss the take-out. CR 278 to Clay Hills can be impassable when wet.
